- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:

path.description: Directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Defaults to the current working directory.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Search file contents using regular expressions (powered by ripgrep).

Use Grep when the task is to find unknown content or unknown file locations. Do not use shell `grep` or `rg` directly; this tool applies workspace path policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
ALWAYS use Grep tool instead of running `grep` or `rg` from a shell — direct shell calls bypass workspace policy, output limits, and sensitive-file filtering.
If you already know a concrete file path and need to inspect its contents, use Read directly instead.

Write patterns in ripgrep regex syntax, which differs from POSIX `grep` syntax. For example, braces are special, so escape them as `\{` to match a literal `{`.

Hidden files (dotfiles such as `.gitlab-ci.yml` or `.eslintrc.json`) are searched by default. To also search files excluded by `.gitignore` (such as `node_modules` or build outputs), set `include_ignored` to `true`. Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always skipped for safety, even when `include_ignored` is `true`.

path.description: File or directory to search. Accepts an absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory. Omit to search the current working directory. Use Read instead when you already know a concrete file path and need its contents.

glob.description: Optional glob filter for which files to search, e.g. `*.ts`. Matched against each file's full absolute path, so a path-anchored pattern like `src/**/*.ts` silently matches nothing — use a basename pattern (`*.ts`), or anchor with `**/` (`**/src/**/*.ts`). To scope the search to a directory, use `path` instead.

type.description: Optional ripgrep file type filter, such as ts or py. Prefer this over `glob` when filtering by language or file kind: it is more efficient and less error-prone than an equivalent glob pattern.

output_mode.description: Shape of the result. `content` shows matching lines (honors `-A`, `-B`, `-C`, `-n`, and `head_limit`); `files_with_matches` shows only the paths of files that contain a match, most-recently-modified first (honors `head_limit`); `count_matches` shows per-file match counts as `path:count` lines, preceded by an aggregate total line. Defaults to `files_with_matches`.

-i.description: Perform a case-insensitive search. Defaults to false.

-n.description: Prefix each matching line with its line number. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`. Defaults to true.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match. Applies only when `output_mode` is `content`; takes precedence over `-A` and `-B`.

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries after offset. Defaults to 250. Pass 0 for unlimited.

offset.description: Number of leading lines/entries to skip before applying `head_limit`. Use it together with `head_limit` to page through large result sets. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline matching, where the pattern can span line boundaries and `.` also matches newlines. Defaults to false.

include_ignored.description: Also search files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Read a text file from the local filesystem.

If the user provides a concrete file path to a text file, call Read directly. Do not `Glob`, `ls`, or otherwise pre-check known text file paths; missing or invalid file paths return errors you can handle. Do not use Read for directories; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob when you need files matching a name pattern (Glob lists files only, never directories). Use `Grep` only when the task is to search for unknown content or locations.

When you need several files, prefer to read them in parallel: emit multiple `Read` calls in a single response instead of reading one file per turn.

- Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute.
- Returns up to 1000 lines or 100 KB per call, whichever comes first; lines longer than 2000 chars are truncated mid-line.
- Page larger files with `line_offset` (1-based start line) and `n_lines`. Omit `n_lines` to read up to the 1000-line cap.
- Sensitive files (`.env` files, credential stores, SSH private keys, and similar secrets) are refused to protect secrets; do not attempt to read them. Templates and public keys are exempt: `.env.example` / `.env.sample` / `.env.template` and public SSH keys such as `id_rsa.pub` read normally.
- Only UTF-8 text files can be read. Non-UTF-8 encodings, binary files, and files containing NUL bytes are refused; use `ReadMediaFile` for images or video, and Bash or an MCP tool for other binary formats.
- Negative line_offset reads from the end of the file (for example, -100 reads the last 100 lines); the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.
- Output format: `<line-number>\t<content>` per line.
- A `<system>...</system>` status block is appended after the file content; it summarizes how much was read (line and byte counts, truncation, line-ending notes) and is not part of the file itself.
- Pure CRLF files are displayed with LF line endings; `Edit` matches this output and preserves CRLF when writing back.
- Mixed or lone carriage-return line endings are shown as `\r` and require exact `Edit.old_string` escapes.
- After a successful `Edit`/`Write`, do not re-read solely to prove the write landed. When the task depends on an exact file, API, or output shape, inspect the final external contract before finishing.

path.description: Path to a text file. Relative paths resolve against the working directory; a path outside the working directory must be absolute. Directories are not supported; use `ls` via Bash for a known directory, or Glob for pattern search.

line_offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Omit to start at line 1. Negative values read from the end of the file; the absolute value cannot exceed 1000.

n_lines.description: The number of lines to read; the tool also applies its internal cap. Omit to read up to the internal cap of 1000 lines.

# `stg refresh` — observed behavior spec (StGit 2.5.5 reference binary)

All observations from running `/workspace/executable` (StGit 2.5.5) in throwaway repos.
Git identity: `Test <t@t.com>`. Exit codes noted per case. `stg refresh` has **no**
`-b/--branch` option and no `--subdir` option (the task brief listed those; they don't
exist — `-s` is `--signoff`, `-F` is `--force`, `-f` is `--file`).

## Usage / flags (from `stg refresh --help`)

```
Usage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...

Arguments:
  [path]...                         Only refresh files matching path

Refresh Options:
  -u, --update                      Only update the current patch files
  -i, --index                       Set patch top to index contents instead of worktree
  -F, --force                       Force full refresh even when index is dirty
      --conflicts[=<policy>]        "allow" (default) or "disallow"
  -p, --patch <patch>               Refresh (applied) <patch> instead of the top patch
  -a, --annotate <note>             Annotate the patch log entry with <note>
      --submodules / --no-submodules

Patch Edit Options:
  -e, --edit                        Invoke editor for patch description
  -d, --diff                        Show diff when editing patch description
  -m, --message <message>           Use message instead of invoking the editor
  -f, --file <path>                 Read message from file ("-" = stdin)
      --no-verify                   Disable commit-msg hook
  -s, --signoff[=<value>]           Add Signed-off-by trailer (repeatable)
      --ack[=<value>]               Add Acked-by trailer (repeatable)
      --review[=<value>]            Add Reviewed-by trailer (repeatable)
      --author <name-and-email>
      --authname <name>
      --authemail <email>
      --authdate <date>             "now" = current time
      --committer-date-is-author-date
```
Plus global `--color <when>` (auto/always/never/ansi), `-h/--help`.

## Core mechanism

Refresh works via a **temporary patch**:
1. A new patch named `refresh-temp` (first free of `refresh-temp`, `refresh-temp-1`,
   `refresh-temp-2`, ...) is created on top of the current top, containing the changes
   to be refreshed. Temp commit message is exactly `Refresh of <target-patch-name>`
   with **no trailing newline**; author/committer = current user @ current time.
2. If the target patch is not the top, patches above it (incl. the temp) are popped,
   the temp is pushed at the target's position.
3. The temp patch is popped and merged ("squashed") into the target patch, which is
   rewritten (new commit).
4. Patches above are re-pushed.

Two stack-log entries per refresh:
- `refresh refresh-temp (create temporary patch)`
- `refresh <target>`  (or `refresh  (CONFLICT)` on conflict — note two spaces; or
  `refresh` when aborting with `--conflicts=disallow`)

So `stg undo` once → back to state with temp patch applied on top; twice → original
state. `--annotate <note>` is appended as the body of the `refresh <target>` log-entry
commit message only (`refresh p1\n\nmy annotation note`); visible in `stg log -f`,
not in plain `stg log`.

## Transaction output markers

stdout, one per line:
- `> <name> (new)` — temp patch created (topmost)
- `- <name>` / `- <first>..<last>` — patch(es) popped (range when >1)
- `> <name>` — patch pushed, now topmost
- `+ <name>` — patch pushed, not topmost
- `# <name>` — temp patch merged away (deleted)
- `& <name>` — target patch updated (rewritten with temp's changes)
- `old => new` — patch renamed (only via editor `Patch:` header)
- Suffixes: ` (new)`, ` (empty)`, ` (conflict)` appended after the name.
- Conflict file status lines (e.g. `UU c.txt`) printed on stdout after the conflict line.

### Canonical sequences (verbatim stdout)

Refresh top patch, with changes:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
> p1
```
Exit 0. If the refreshed commit is identical (clean worktree, no message options),
the `& p1` line is omitted, the commit is **not** rewritten, exit still 0:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
> p1
```

Refresh non-top applied patch (`stg refresh -p p1`, p1 below p2,p3):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp
- refresh-temp
# refresh-temp
& p1
+ p2
> p3
```
(Patches above target popped together with temp in one range, temp pushed at target
position, merged, then others re-pushed. Pushed empty patches get ` (empty)` suffix,
e.g. `+ refresh-temp (empty)`. If the temp ends up empty at the target position the
topmost line reads `> refresh-temp (empty)` and `&` is omitted.)

Refresh an **unapplied** patch (`-p` accepts unapplied patches; works even with all
patches popped, provided the temp patch is creatable from worktree vs HEAD):
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- refresh-temp
& p2
# refresh-temp
> p1
```
Note order: `& <target>` **before** `# refresh-temp`; trailing `> p1` only if there is
an applied topmost patch (omitted when all popped). If nothing changed, the `&` line
is omitted too.

## Dirty-index check

- Staged-only changes (worktree == index ≠ HEAD): refresh proceeds, no warning.
- Unstaged-only changes: proceeds.
- Staged **and** unstaged changes present (any files, even different files):
  ```
  error: the index is dirty; consider using `--index` or `--force`
  ```
  stderr, exit 2, no output on stdout, no side effects. `-F/--force` or `-i/--index`
  override. Untracked files don't count as changes and are never refreshed.

## `--index` / `--update` / pathspecs

- `--index`: patch top set to index contents; unstaged worktree changes preserved.
- `-u/--update`: only files already in the target patch are refreshed; other staged
  files stay staged. (Dirty-index check still applies.)
- Pathspecs are relative to **cwd**; only matching files are refreshed, the rest stay
  staged/unstaged. Pathspec matching nothing → success (exit 0), output without `&`.
- Running from a subdirectory with **no** pathspec refreshes everything (cwd does not
  limit scope).
- Deletions (staged `git rm` or unstaged `rm`) are refreshed like other changes.

## Errors (stderr, exit codes)

| Case | Message | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| No applied patches (default target) | `error: no patches applied` | 2 |
| `-p` nonexistent | ``error: patch `nosuch` does not exist`` | 2 |
| `-p` hidden patch | ``error: hidden patch `p2` is not allowed`` | 2 |
| Detached HEAD | `error: not on branch, HEAD is detached` | 2 |
| `-p branch:name` syntax | `error: invalid value 'other:op' for '--patch <patch>': invalid patch locator ` + backtick-quoted `other:op` + `\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--authdate` | `error: invalid value 'garbage' for '--authdate <date>': invalid date `garbage`` + blank + `For more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| Bad `--author` | `error: invalid value 'NoEmail' for '--author <name-and-email>': invalid name and email `NoEmail`` + help line | 1 |
| `-m` twice | `error: the argument '--message <message>' cannot be used multiple times` + `\n\nUsage: stg refresh [OPTIONS] [path]...\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.` | 1 |
| `-m ""` | `error: a value is required for '--message <message>' but none was supplied` + help line | 1 |
| Merge conflict (allow) | `error: merge conflicts; resolve conflicts manually then refresh or undo the operation with `stg undo --hard`.` | 3 |
| `--conflicts=disallow` | ``error: pushing patch `refresh-temp` would result in conflicts and push conflicts are disallowed`` | 3 |
| commit-msg hook fails | `<hook stderr>` then ``error: `commit-msg` hook returned 1`` | 2 |
| Empty message from editor | `error: aborting due to empty patch description` | 2 |
| Editor fails to run | `error: running editor: vi: No such file or directory (os error 2)` (falls back to `vi` when no EDITOR) | 2 |

## Conflict behavior (`refresh -p p1` conflicting with p2 above)

stdout:
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
> refresh-temp (conflict)
UU c.txt
```
stderr: `error: merge conflicts; ...` (above), exit 3.
State: temp patch left **applied and topmost**, patches above target unapplied
(`+ p1`, `> refresh-temp`, `- p2`); stack-log entry `refresh  (CONFLICT)`.
Conflict markers: `<<<<<<< current` / `=======` / `>>>>>>> patched`.
Resolution flow: fix files, `git add`, plain `stg refresh` (refreshes the temp patch,
new temp named `refresh-temp-1`), then `stg squash`/`stg push` etc.

With `--conflicts=disallow` (or `stgit.push.allow-conflicts=false`): stdout stops at
```
> refresh-temp (new)
- p2..refresh-temp
```
exit 3, temp patch left **unapplied** in the stack, target topmost applied.

On aborts (hook failure, empty editor message, editor spawn failure): only
`> refresh-temp (new)` is printed and the temp patch remains applied/topmost.

## Commit rewriting semantics

- Plain refresh preserves author name/email/date of the original patch commit;
  committer = current user, committer date = now.
- `--author "N <e>"`, `--authname`, `--authemail`, `--authdate` (accepts e.g.
  `2001-02-03T04:05:06`, `1999-12-31 23:59:59`, `now`) override the corresponding
  author fields; unspecified fields keep previous values.
- `--committer-date-is-author-date`: committer timestamp = author timestamp.
- `-m/--message`, `-f/--file` (`-` = stdin), `-e/--edit` replace the patch message.
  `-m` with no content changes still rewrites the commit (`&` shown).
- Trailers: `-s/--signoff`, `--ack`, `--review` default to committer identity; custom
  values require `=` syntax (`--signoff="Custom Signer <cs@x.com>"`) — a space-separated
  value is treated as a pathspec positional. Appended to existing trailers; exact
  duplicate trailers are suppressed (repeat `-s -s` adds one).
- `stgit.autosign` config: no effect observed on refresh.
- Resulting patch may become empty — allowed, kept in stack.

## Editor (`-e`)

- `hint: Waiting for your editor to close the file...` printed to **stderr**.
- Editor template:
  ```
  Patch:  p1
  Author: Test <t@t.com>
  Date:   2026-08-07 12:17:06 +0000

  <current message>

  # Please enter the message for your patch. Lines starting with
  # '#' will be ignored. An empty message aborts the new patch.
  # The patch name and author information may also be modified.
  # The diff below is for reference. Any edits will be ignored.
  # ------------------------ >8 ------------------------
  # Do not modify or remove the line above.
  <diff, only with -d>
  ```
- Editing the `Patch:` header renames the patch: output gains `p1 => renamed` after
  the `& p1` line and ends `> renamed`.
- Editing `Author:` header changes the author.
- `-d` appends the **full patch diff** (40-char blob hashes) after the `>8` cut line;
  `-d` without `-e` is silently ignored.
- `-m` + `-e`: editor starts from the `-m` message.
- Empty resulting message → abort (exit 2, temp patch left).

## commit-msg hook

- Runs **only when message options are given** (`-m`/`-e`/`-f`/trailers), once, on a
  temp file `.stgit-msg-temp-<pid>` in the repo root (removed afterwards); hook edits
  to the file take effect. Does not run on plain content-only refresh. `--no-verify`
  skips it. Nonzero hook exit aborts (exit 2, temp patch left applied).

## Color output (`--color always`, raw escapes)

Each line begins with `\033[0m`; after the final line a trailing `\033[0m` is emitted.
- `> name (new)`: `\033[34m> \033[0m` `\033[1mname\033[0m` `\033[0m\033[33m (new)\n`
- `> name` (topmost, normal): `\033[34m> \033[0m\033[1mname\n` (bold name)
- `> name` (conflict): `\033[31m> \033[0m\033[1mname\033[0m\033[0m\033[33m (conflict)\n`
